{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Transit systems nationwide are under severe financial stress because of the pandemic.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Transit systems are incurring additional expenditures for frequent sanitization of handrails, benches, seats, and other surfaces that employees and passengers touch frequently.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"On many transit systems, buses are operating free with rear-door entry to protect operators and passengers from being in close proximity, since the farebox is typically located right next to the driver.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"As of 2018, transit farebox revenue from passengers nationwide was about $20 billion.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"If only half of the $20 billion in transit farebox revenue is foregone, transit agencies nationwide will be in the hole by $10 billion.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"A sanitized and monitored bus is safer than a possibly contaminated cab or on-demand vehicle which may have served dozens of other passengers.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Frequent, reliable, free service is essential both for reasons of public health and needed economic relief.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
